svg.title: From Treasury Record to Recognized Service Fee
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-evidence-to-service-fee; chart type: process_flow; title: From Treasury Record to Recognized Service Fee; subtitle: Five operating stages separate client assets from operator earnings.; chapter number: 1; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Use authorized public records and owner-provided evidence. A matching name is only a lead, not proof of entitlement. The canonical first-deal planning window is 3–12 months; filing does not establish a payment date.; caption: State-held principal belongs to the owner. Recognize only earned service fees under the applicable accounting policy.; stages: label: Source eligible records; value: Capture the official record and custody dates; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Record treasury jurisdiction, property identifier, holder, reported owner, and available dates in SQLite. Preserve source links and follow the portal's access conditions.; label: Resolve ownership; value: Build an evidence-backed owner identity chain; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Compare addresses, entity filings, name changes, and signer authority. Escalate mergers, estates, and dissolved entities instead of treating fuzzy matches as ownership.; label: Qualify the engagement; value: Check finder rules before compensated recovery work; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Document registration requirements, permitted contracting dates, fee limits, and required agreement terms. Explain the owner's direct-claim option before requesting signature.; label: Submit and track; value: File authorized evidence through the treasury channel; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Use the state's accepted claimant or representative process. Log receipt identifiers, evidence requests, response deadlines, and owner-authorized status checks.; label: Reconcile and bill; value: Separate owner proceeds from earned service fees; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Prefer treasury payment directly to the owner. Confirm the contractual earning event, invoice the permitted fee, and reconcile fee receivables separately from client principal.

Assumptions: Use authorized public records and owner-provided evidence. A matching name is only a lead, not proof of entitlement. The canonical first-deal planning window is 3–12 months; filing does not establish a payment date.
